metadata.title: Joe Burrow throws two TDs in Week 11 loss
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 28 of his 40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a 22-20 loss to the Commanders in Week 11.
metadata.analysis: Burrow and the Cincy offense got off to a slow start on a rainy night at Northwest Stadium as they didn't score their first points until the second quarter.  His first touchdown pass went to Tee Higgins in the second quarter, while his second was a four-yard completion to Colbie Young in the third. The game on Monday night was the first time Burrow didn't throw for at least three touchdowns since Week 4 vs. Jacksonville. He will be a top-three fantasy QB in Week 12 against the Saints.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Throws Two Touchdowns in Bengals' Loss
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow had a solid game with exactly 300 passing yards and two passing touchdowns, but it wasn't enough to get the win on a rainy night in Washington, D.C. The Commanders rallied back with five second-half field goals to get the win on Monday Night Football, snapping Cincinnati's five-game winning streak. Burrow completed 28 of 40 pass attempts and added two carries for a loss of one yard. After heavy rain in the first quarter, Burrow connected with Tee Higgins on a 31-yard touchdown just after the two-minute warning in the second quarter. After halftime, he found Colbie Young for a four-yard touchdown while under pressure. He leaned heavily on shorter passes to his RBs and TEs and wasn't able to get into a rhythm with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins downfield. His 300 yards and two touchdowns were still solid numbers, but his performance snapped a streak of five straight games with at least four total touchdowns. He's still a top-shelf option at QB next week at home against the Saints, in a matchup that should help the Bengals' offense quickly put Monday's disappointing outcome behind them.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Another 300-yard effort in loss
metadata.description: Burrow completed 28 of 40 passes for 300 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 22-20 loss to the Commanders on Monday night.
metadata.analysis: The Bengals' offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Poised For Another Huge Game In Week 11
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow continued his red hot streak in last week's 38-18 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Burrow completed 35 of 44 pass attempts (80%) for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the blowout win. The Bengals QB has easily been the most valuable quarterback in fantasy over this recent stretch and he will get the opportunity to continue lighting up the box score this Monday night. Burrow and the Bengals will head to Washington to take on the Commanders in prime time. The Commanders defense has not been especially tough on quarterbacks this season and Burrow is playing as well as anyone right now so the matchup should not hold him back. This contest is also tied for the highest over/under of the week, meaning there should be a lot of points on the board when the game ends. Burrow is ranked QB1 in our RotoBaller Week 11 rankings, making him an easy start at the position. Burrow has been playing incredible football lately and he should continue being productive this Monday night.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Officially cleared for Monday Night Football
metadata.description: Burrow (illness) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Commanders.
metadata.analysis: Burrow dealt with an illness during Week 11 prep, but with no injury tag the 2020 first overall pick has been officially cleared to play Monday night -- and per ESPN.com he is confident he will do so at "full strength." He's thrown at least three touchdowns in each of his last five outings, and over that span he has completed 77.6 percent of his passes for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns and three interceptions while turning 13 carries into 47 yards and two scores. The Bengals will face a Commanders defense that ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (244.8) and 30th in red-zone touchdown rate (71.9 percent).

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Carries No Injury Designation for Monday Night
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) carries no game designation for Monday night's matchup with the Washington Commanders. He practiced in full at each of Cincinnati's three sessions from Thursday through Saturday and said Friday that he was feeling better. Wide receiver Tee Higgins (knee) is set to play after three full practices. His 824 receiving yards rank sixth in the NFL, two spots behind Ja'Marr Chase. The Bengals will be without starting right guard Dalton Risner (knees) against a defense that blitzes at the NFL's fourth-highest rate (35.7%), according to Pro Football Reference. Burrow completed all 12 of his attempts against the Pittsburgh Steelers' blitz for 186 yards in Week 10, per Next Gen Stats. He finished with 409 passing yards and four touchdowns, his fifth straight game with at least three touchdown passes. Washington ranks 31st with 244.8 net passing yards allowed per game and gave up 293 passing yards to New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy in its last game. Burrow is RotoBaller's top-ranked quarterback for Week 11.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Expects to be full strength for MNF
metadata.description: Burrow (illness) said Friday that he's getting better, noting that he "for sure" feels optimistic he'll be at full strength for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer reports.
metadata.analysis: Burrow is managing what the Bengals list as an illness, but the QB was a full participant in Thursday's practice, and is trending toward approaching Monday night's game without a Week 11 designation. Official confirmation of that expected outcome will arrive Saturday, either way.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow (illness) practicing Friday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow is practicing on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow had missed his press conference on Thursday due to an illness. He appears to still be trending towards being good to go for Monday's game against the Commanders.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Optimistic He'll be at Full Strength Monday Night
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) said he feels optimistic that he will be at full strength for his team's Week 11 matchup against the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football, per Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer. Burrow is dealing with an illness, but he has participated in practice this week and seems unlikely to be facing any sort of restriction on Monday night. The 29-year-old has emerged as the NFL's MVP frontrunner in 2026, completing 74.7% of his pass attempts for 2,795 yards, 27 touchdowns, and six interceptions across nine games. Burrow has played at a preposterously high level lately, throwing for over 1,600 yards and 20 touchdowns over his last five starts. As long as he's active, Burrow profiles as an elite quarterback option for fantasy managers in Week 11.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Turns in full practice Thursday
metadata.description: Burrow (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: After appearing on the injury report with an illness, Burrow's full practice Thursday suggests the Bengals quarterback isn't facing any obvious limitations ahead of Monday night's date with the Commanders. A frontrunner in the MVP conversation, Burrow has been playing lights-out football for the past month-plus, as he and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are firing on all cylinders.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Practices Fully Despite Illness on Thursday
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was under the weather on Thursday, but he still managed to put in a full practice, according to Jay Morrison of BengalsTalk.com. Fantasy managers should not have anything to worry about with Burrow as the team prepares for a Monday night clash in Week 11 on the road against the Washington Commanders. The 29-year-old should be feeling much better by Monday's contest, and after the historic run that he has been on of late, he needs to be in all starting fantasy lineups. The three-time Pro Bowler has been on a tear since Week 5, throwing at least three touchdowns in five straight games, including four touchdown passes in three of those contests. In all, Burrow has thrown for 1,624 yards, 20 touchdowns, and only three interceptions in that span to help the Bengals go 5-0. The fantastic stretch has vaulted him above Josh Allen for the title of QB1 in fantasy through the first 10 weeks of the 2026 season with 2,795 passing yards, 27 touchdowns, and only six interceptions in nine starts. Burrow should be able to pick apart the Commanders' secondary on Monday night as he looks to add to his torrid stretch.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Having the Best Season of His Career
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is in the midst of a career year. The former No. 1 pick ranks as the overall QB1 in fantasy scoring, has emerged as the frontrunner for the MVP award, and has the Bengals sitting at 7-2, which gives them sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Burrow has been impressive all year long, but his last five games have been truly on another level. He has 4+ touchdowns in each of his last five games, becoming only the second quarterback in NFL history to accomplish that feat. He's up to 2,795 passing yards, 30 total touchdowns, and just six interceptions (three of which came in one game). The 29-year-old has benefitted from the presence of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, although he has also shown he can spread the ball around when needed, targeting players like Chase Brown, Mike Gesicki, or Dohnte Meyers. As long as he stays healthy, Burrow shows no signs of slowing down. He should continue to be started as a high-end QB1 in all fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow dominant in win Sunday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 35-of-44 passing attempts for 409 yards and four touchdowns in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Burrow had another unreal performance on Sunday night. He took on a tough Pittsburgh defense, but he was able to come away with over 400 yards and four touchdowns en route to a win, while also committing zero turnovers in the process. He has been playing some of the best football in the league recently and will certainly be an MVP finalist if he can continue on a similar pace over the back half of the season.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Record-tying performance in win
metadata.description: Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added one rush for eight yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night.
metadata.analysis: The latest installment in what is looking like an MVP-worthy campaign for Burrow included quite a milestone, as the 2020 first overall pick became the only other player in NFL history beside Peyton Manning in 2004 to score four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. All of Burrow's scores Sunday night came through the air, as he connected with Drew Sample (three yards), Chase Brown (two, four yards) and Dohnte Meyers (15 yards) for his quartet of TD strikes. Burrow also found the bulk of his success when focusing on top wideout Ja'Marr Chase, who was responsible for 11 of Burrow's completions and 231 of his yards on 14 targets. Burrow has now exceeded 400 passing yards on three occasions this season, including twice in the last three games, heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Commanders on Monday night, Nov. 23.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Rewrites History Books with Four More Touchdowns on Sunday
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow completed 35 of his 44 pass attempts for 409 yards, four passing touchdowns, and zero turnovers during Sunday's Week 10 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He also rushed for eight yards and took just one sack. Burrow has been absolutely magnificent lately, becoming just the second player in NFL history to record 4+ touchdowns in five consecutive games. Over his last five contests, he has posted a whopping 1,624 passing yards and 22 total touchdowns. He has also played turnover-free football in four of those five games. The former No. 1 pick has officially taken over as the overall QB1 in fantasy scoring, passing Josh Allen for the top spot on Sunday. Burrow has benefitted from a supporting cast headlined by Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. As long as Burrow, Chase, and Higgins stay healthy, the LSU product will remain a high-end QB1 on a weekly basis. He should continue to dominate in Week 11 against the Washington Commanders, who just allowed 293 passing yards to J.J. McCarthy.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Ready To Take On AFC North Rivals In Week 10
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers at home this Sunday night. Burrow and the Bengals have been on quite the heater over the past month, rattling off four straight wins and scoring over 30 points in every game. The superstar quarterback has been especially hot as he's thrown 16 touchdowns and passed for 1,215 yards in that span, averaging four passing touchdowns and over 303 passing yards a game. Burrow will now face a tough Steelers defense as the teams battle it out for first place in the AFC North division. The Pittsburgh defense features a fierce pass rush and a solid secondary, but Burrow has been playing too well to even think about sitting him this week. Burrow is ranked QB3 in our RotoBaller Week 10 rankings, making him a must-start option at the position this Sunday night.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Making a Push for Overall QB1 Spot in Fantasy Football
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been on fire lately, and he's making a push to rank as the overall QB1 in total scoring. Burrow has a whopping 18 touchdowns and just three turnovers over his last four games, and the fact that he is already past his bye week bodes well for his overall fantasy point total as the season goes on. Furthermore, the Bengals' star quarterback has managed to stay healthy this season, which is a refreshing improvement from 2023 and 2025. While we're only halfway through the 2026 campaign, we're hopeful that Burrow can stay healthy and strengthen his push to be the top-scoring quarterback in fantasy football for the first time in his career. As it stands, his previous career-high finish was QB3 in 2023. Burrow certainly has the supporting cast to accomplish that feat, as Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase have both been top-eight fantasy receivers in PPR leagues amid a remarkable start to the season. A relatively tough matchup awaits Burrow this week in the form of the Steelers, but then he gets a softer schedule with games against the Commanders, Saints, and Browns. A Week 14 matchup against the Chiefs has shootout potential, and then he should coast throughout the fantasy playoffs against the Panthers, Colts, and Ravens. Just when it seemed like Burrow's ceiling couldn't get any higher, he continues to trend up in fantasy football.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow tosses three touchdowns in Week 9 win
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 pass attempts for 271 yards and three touchdowns in a 34-17 win over the Falcons. Burrow also rushed for seven yards and a touchdown on three attempts.
metadata.analysis: Burrow found Ja'Marr Chase once and Tee Higgins twice for his three passing touchdowns in another stellar performance. Burrow has at least three passing touchdowns in each of his last four games. The Bengals will look to continue their strong play against the Steelers in Week 10.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Another stellar effort in Week 9 win
metadata.description: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.
metadata.analysis: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Delivers Elite Fantasy Value on Fewer Throws
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw 19 fewer passes than he did against the Tennessee Titans last week and still accounted for every Cincinnati touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 Week 9 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. Burrow went 24-for-29 for 271 yards with three touchdown passes and no interceptions. Ja'Marr Chase supplied more than half of those yards, finishing with 155 and scoring from 47 yards out. His other three touchdowns came from inside the 10-yard line. He scored on a one-yard sneak, his second rushing touchdown in as many games, and hit Tee Higgins from four and eight yards out. The second Higgins score came on the drive after Atlanta cut the lead to seven in the third quarter. Burrow has thrown 12 touchdown passes over his last three games, with two of those outings coming on 30 attempts or fewer. He's an elite QB1 for the Week 10 home rematch with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who gave up 282 passing yards and three touchdowns to him in Week 3.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Should Continue Hot Stretch Against Atlanta
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been on quite the heater over his last three games, with the latest being his best game yet. Burrow has now rattled off three straight games with four passing touchdowns and passed for 462 yards in last week's overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. With the offense playing this well, they should keep rolling as they head to Madrid to face the Atlanta Falcons. The Falcons' defense has been tough against most quarterbacks this season, but given his talent and the talent around him, Burrow should be able to overcome the matchup. Another positive is that this matchup is currently the week's highest over/under, set at 52.5 points as of Friday. Burrow has been firing on all cylinders lately and should continue to do so in what could be a high-scoring affair. Burrow is ranked QB1 in our RotoBaller Week 9 rankings, making him the top option at the position this Sunday. Fantasy managers should feel confident plugging Burrow into lineups again this weekend.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow throws five TDs, three INTs in Week 8 win
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 38 of his 48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns, and three interceptions while adding three rushes for 10 yards and a touchdown on the ground in a 43-36 overtime win over the Titans in Week 8.
metadata.analysis: Burrow turned in a huge game as the Titans surprisingly gave the Bengals all they could handle. The Cincy quarterback is heating up of late as he's thrown 13 touchdowns over his past three contests. Overall, Burrow has 20 touchdowns and six interceptions through seven games. He will be a high-end QB1 in Week 8 vs. the Falcons.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Six total TDs in wild win
metadata.description: Burrow completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions and added three carries for 10 yards and another score in the Bengals' 43-36 overtime win over the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: A Titans offense that had been mostly moribund all season unexpectedly came to life Sunday, requiring Burrow to remain aggressive throughout the afternoon. While that helped lead to his season-high three interceptions, it was also unsurprisingly a boon for his fantasy production, as the 2020 first overall pick finished with his second 400-yard performance of the season and a season-high five TD tosses. Burrow had his connection with top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins working throughout the afternoon, as he connected with the duo a combined 21 times for 296 yards and three touchdowns. Burrow's other two scoring strikes went to Mike Gesicki and Jack Endries, and the prolific quarterback then sealed the win himself with a nine-yard scoring run at the seven-minute mark of overtime. Burrow and the Bengals now make the transatlantic flight to Madrid, Spain, where they'll face the Falcons next Sunday in a Week 9 matchup.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Lights Up Titans in Overtime Victory
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow picked apart the Tennessee Titans defense in a 43-36 overtime victory in Week 8. Burrow completed 38 out of 48 pass attempts (79.2%) for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions, while adding 10 rushing yards and an additional touchdown on the ground. The yards and touchdown passes were both a season-high for Burrow, although the three picks were the most he has thrown in a game in 2026 as well. Burrow engineered a game-tying touchdown drive with 1:11 to go in the game, finding wide receiver Tee Higgins for an 18-yard score. In overtime, Burrow had what ultimately became a game-winning nine-yard touchdown run. Burrow connected with Higgins for 10 receptions for 155 yards and a touchdown, and found fellow wideout Ja'Marr Chase 11 times for 141 yards and a touchdown. Burrow's strong 2026 campaign continues, and he remains locked in as a strong QB1.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Ready To Continue Hot Streak In Week 8
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will face the Tennessee Titans at home in Week 8. Burrow has been one of the best fantasy quarterbacks since Week 3, scoring at least 22 points every week in 4-point per passing touchdown leagues. The Bengals star sandwiched the team's Week 6 bye with four-touchdown performances in Weeks 5 and 7. Burrow passed for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens last week. The LSU alum will get the chance to continue his strong play against the Titans in Cincinnati. The Tennessee defense has been an easy matchup for opposing quarterbacks this season so Burrow is set up to smash yet again. Burrow is ranked QB3 in our RotoBaller Week 8 rankings, making him one of the best options at the position this week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Dominant performance in second half
metadata.description: Burrow completed 22 of 30 passes for 292 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 12 yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow couldn't lead the Bengals to a single point in the first half, but the 2020 first overall pick came out of intermission locked in. Burrow helped spearhead five consecutive scoring drives to start the second half, capping four of them with touchdown passes to Mike Gesicki (six yards), Tee Higgins (13 yards), Ja'Marr Chase (two yards ) and Drew Sample (16 yards). The game marked Burrow's second straight with four scoring tosses and zero interceptions, and both his passing yardage total and 73.3 percent completion rate were both his second highest of the season. Burrow will take 1,653 passing yards and a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow tosses four touchdowns in Week 7 win
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 22-of-30 passes for 292 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens. He rushed for 12 yards on two carries.
metadata.analysis: Burrow and the Bengals' offense came alive in the second half, erasing a 13-0 deficit with a 35 point performance to close out the comeback win. Burrow has eight touchdown passes in his last two games and will look to continue his recent strong play against the Titans in Week 8.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Leads Stellar Second-Half Comeback
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was sluggish to begin the game as this offense was held to zero points in the first half of Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens. Burrow locked in at halftime and put together an excellent second half. Overall, Burrow completed 22-of-30 passing attempts for 292 passing yards with four touchdowns and zero interceptions in the comeback win. The 29-year-old put together five straight scoring drives to help get his team a big Week 7 victory. Over his last two games, Burrow has thrown for eight touchdowns without any interceptions. He'll look to keep up this excellent play against the Tennessee Titans in Week 8.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow With A Juicy Matchup In Week 7
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will lead the team against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7. Burrow is fresh off the team's bye week and ready to face off against a division rival. When the Bengals were last active, Burrow tossed four passing touchdowns in a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins. The veteran QB will look to pick up where he left off on the road in Baltimore. The Ravens defense has been one of the easier matchups for opposing quarterbacks this season, putting Burrow in a very advantageous position this Sunday. Burrow should be able to connect with his top receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins often throughout what could be a high-scoring affair. Burrow is ranked QB6 in our RotoBaller Week 7 rankings, making him a strong QB1 option this Sunday. Fantasy managers should be excited to plug Burrow back into lineups this week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow throws four touchdowns in win Sunday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 23-of-32 passing attempts for 190 yards and four touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Burrow looked great on Sunday. He scored four touchdowns through the air en route to a win over the Dolphins, which left him with a great fantasy total on the day. The Bengals are now heading into their bye week but he should continue to be a great fantasy option when the team is back out on the field.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Offsets modest yardage with TDs
metadata.description: Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for 10 yards in the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow averaged only 5.9 yards per attempt and finished with a season-low passing yardage total, but he offset the modest numbers by throwing a season-high number of touchdown passes. The prolific signal-caller benefited from having both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins available after each carried questionable designations into Sunday, and he connected with Mike Gesicki (four yards), Samaje Perine (six yards), Tanner Hudson (two yards) and Ja'Marr Chase (45 yards) four his quartet of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, and he'll take an 11:3 TD:INT into a Week 7 road matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 25 following a Week 6 bye.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Could Be Missing Key Pieces In Week 5
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Miami Dolphins with a hobbled offense in Week 5. Burrow passed for 428 yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions in the 17-22 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week. Bengals star receiver Ja'Marr Chase left early in that contest with a concussion, and fellow wideout Tee Higgins also left with a groin injury. Burrow will now head into Miami with his two top pass catchers questionable to play. Despite potentially having a diminished receiving corps, the Bengals QB should be in line for a productive game due to the matchup. The Dolphins defense is among the worst in the league, so the Bengals offense should have no issues scoring against them. The only thing that fantasy managers will need to worry about is whether Burrow and the Bengals will need to continue throwing later into the game. The Bengals are heavy road favorites despite the injuries they're dealing with, which is a testament to the weakness of the Miami offense and the improvement of the Cincinnati defense. If the Bengals run out to an early lead, Burrow may be content with handing the ball off to Chase Brown over and over. Burrow is ranked QB5 in our RotoBaller Week 5 rankings, making him a strong QB1 option in a soft matchup. Fantasy managers should still start Burrow without his top weapons, but his ceiling may be lower than usual this week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow throws two interceptions Sunday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passing attempts for 428 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions while adding six yards and a touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Burrow had an up-and-down performance on Sunday. On the one hand, he was able to throw for over 425 yards and logged two total touchdowns against the Jaguars. On the other hand, he threw two interceptions and led Cincinnati to score just 17 points in a loss at home. His fantasy value for next week will heavily depend on the health of Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) for their matchup against the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Looks Incredible in Loss
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was impressive through the air on Sunday. Burrow completed 39-of-54 passing attempts for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Burrow also rushed the ball three times for six yards and an additional score. It's almost more impressive that Burrow posted these numbers with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) not playing in the second half. Burrow did everything he could, with six different players having at least three receptions during this game. Sadly, both Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) left the game, and Burrow wasn't able to make a comeback. Fantasy managers should consider Burrow an elite fantasy option for the Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Stellar numbers in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Burrow completed 39 of 54 passes for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while rushing three times for six yards and another score in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Cincinnati.
metadata.analysis: Burrow's passing yardage total was made all the more noteworthy by the fact he lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in the first half. The prolific 2020 first-round pick put up new season highs in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, while also generating his first multi-interception tally of the campaign. The first of Burrow's picks came right after the two-minute warning in the first half at the Jaguars' 37-yard line and led to a Jacksonville touchdown. Nevertheless, he continued to battle as the Bengals trailed throughout the rest of the contest, and despite also losing Tee Higgins to an adductor injury with just under six minutes remaining, Burrow drove Cincinnati all the way down to the Jags' nine-yard line before losing the ball on downs with 56 seconds remaining. Prior to that point, Burrow had put his team in position for a potential game-winning touchdown via a 15-yard scoring toss to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter and a one-yard QB sneak with just over three minutes remaining for his first rushing score of the season. Burrow and the Bengals will look to regroup and get Chase and Higgins back for a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Ready For High-Scoring Matchup On Sunday
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in Week 4. Burrow completed 28 of his 37 pass attempts (76%) for 286 yards and three touchdowns in the 27-30 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Despite putting up his best fantasy performance of the season, Burrow and the Bengals walked away with their first loss of the year last week. Cincinnati may have a difficult time getting back in the win column this week at home against the Jaguars. The Jacksonville defense has held opposing offenses to 10 points or fewer in two of their three games this season while racking up eight sacks and four interceptions. The Jaguars offense has also been potent to start the year, scoring about 27 points per game through three games. Burrow and the high-powered Bengals offense will have their hands full in this matchup, but should still be able to put up points in what could turn into a high-scoring game. This game is tied for the week's highest over/under, set at 51.5 points as of Friday. Even with a difficult matchup, Burrow is ranked QB5 in our RotoBaller Week 4 rankings. Fantasy managers should be excited for the potential of this game turning into a back-and-forth affair.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow tosses three touchdowns in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He rushed for 13 yards on two carries.
metadata.analysis: Burrow was excellent for the majority of the game Sunday, finding Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki for his three touchdown passes. The veteran did fumble on what would be the final drive for the Bengals, sealing the win for the Steelers. Burrow and the Bengals will welcome the Jaguars to town in Week 4.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Critical turnover sullies solid day
metadata.description: Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 13 yards in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Burrow was impressive throughout the majority of the afternoon, taking just one sack from Pittsburgh's aggressive defense and connecting with Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki for his trio of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall on an afternoon he entered already down Andrei Iosivas (IR, thumb) and during which he then lost promising rookie Colbie Young (knee). However, a would-be game-tying or game-winning drive was also short-circuited by the franchise signal-caller, as he lost the handle on the ball on a sack with under a minute remaining, snuffing out any chance of Cincinnati being able to at least force overtime. The highly untimely turnover aside, Burrow has looked comfortable with an offensive approach that has him under center more often than previous seasons, and he'll next take aim at the Jaguars in a Week 4 home matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Facing Tough Steelers Defense In Week 3
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 3. Burrow passed for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the 20-6 win over the Houston Texans last week and will try to build on that success this week. The Bengals star took a step back in terms of yardage perspective in Week 2, throwing 47 fewer passing yards, but his touchdown total increased and he didn't throw any picks in his second game. Burrow will try to build on the touchdown success while increasing the yardage against a tough Steelers defense. Through two games, Pittsburgh has allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards and the ninth-most rushing yards. If that trend continues, Burrow could be in for another low-yardage outing on Sunday. The Bengals have the skill players to overcome nearly every matchup, so Burrow has the potential to exceed expectations, but it will not be a cakewalk matchup. It should also be noted that Burrow was not listed on the Bengals injury report this week, signaling that the back issue is now behind him. Burrow is ranked QB9 in our RotoBaller Week 3 rankings, making him a low-end QB1 this Sunday. Fantasy managers should be encouraged by Burrow's upward trend in fantasy scoring, but may need to temper expectations against Pittsburgh.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Solid, mistake-free effort in win
metadata.description: Burrow (back) completed 20 of 31 passes for 207 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding one rush for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow's workmanlike stat line underscores the type of road upset victory it was for the Bengals, who didn't need to be overly aggressive against a Texans offense missing Nico Collins (hamstring). Burrow, who came into the game dealing with back tightness, took his share of lumps in the form of five sacks, but he delivered dynamic 32- and 18-yard touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase. Burrow also notably avoided any turnovers despite being consistently under duress, and through his first two games, he's completed a solid 68.2 percent of his passes and posted three touchdowns versus one interception while operating under center more often than in recent seasons. Burrow will look to continue his solid early-season play in a Week 3 divisional road matchup against the Steelers next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Throws Two Touchdowns In Win Over Texans
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow completed 20 of his 31 pass attempts (65%) for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the 20-6 victory over the Houston Texans. Despite being questionable with a back issue heading into this game, Burrow was able to do enough to pull out a win against a strong Texans defense. Burrow was sacked five times in the contest but stayed in, which is a good sign for his health moving forward. Burrow will look to keep the wins rolling against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. The Steelers defense has racked up seven sacks, three interceptions, and a fumble recovery through two games this season, so Burrow could have his work cut out for him with a tough matchup. That said, the Bengals star QB just took on the strong Texans defense and was successful, so fantasy managers should be confident in his ability heading into next week. Burrow should be considered a strong QB1 for the upcoming week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Expected to Start Against the Texans in Week 2
